paper_metadata.title: Achieving advanced isotropic mechanical properties in a novel L-DED near-α titanium alloy with synergistic alloying modification of Si and B

evidence.quote: This study used a synergistic alloying modification of Si and B to promote the columnar to equiaxed transition (CET) of β grains in L-DED near- α titanium alloy Ti6242S.
The L-DED Ti6242S specimen exhibits millimeter-sized columnar β grains, growing along the building direction ( Fig. 3 a1).

The comparison of the room-temperature tensile properties reveals that the 0.16Si0.05B alloy, with synergistic alloying of Si and B elements, has an optimal combination of strength and plasticity, exhibiting a notable increase in strength while maintaining plasticity.

For the 0.16Si0.05B alloy deposit, the transverse and longitudinal yield strengths and ultimate tensile strengths are intermediate between those of the 0.54Si and 0.1B alloy deposits, and the elongation is comparable to the longitudinal elongation of Ti6242S alloy.
The strength and elongation of the 0.1B and 0.16Si0.05B alloy deposits are both approaching isotropy.

This paper uses Ti6242S (Ti-6Al-2Sn-4Zr-2Mo-0.1Si) near- α high- temperature titanium alloy as the matrix and proposes a novel design strategy for L-DED near- α titanium alloy based on a synergistic alloying modification of Si and B elements.
